To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of VAP varies greatly depending on setting, diagnostic criteria, and patient population; that the mortality attributable to VAP is around10%; that microbiological confirmation of infection should be strongly encouraged; that emerging microbiological tools will modify the way VAP is diagnosed and treated in the next future; that prevention of VAP should include minimizing the exposure to invasive mechanical ventilation, early liberation from mechanical ventilation, and the use of bundles; and that VAP should be treated for a limited period of time

VAP is a common and serious complication of mechanical ventilation, it is associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation and ICU length of stay, and it is associated with an estimated attributable mortality of 10%.
VAP is a frequent complication of mechanical ventilation, associated with prolonged ICU and hospital stay and increased mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new technologies to improve the diagnosis, treatment, prevention and surveillance of ventilator associated pneumonia.
the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of VAP in adults.
understanding the mechanisms of VAP, developing new diagnostic tools to improve the diagnosis and management of VAP and developing strategies to prevent VAP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VAP is a common complication in the ICU that should be prevented, diagnosed, and treated according to a standardized approach.
VAP is a common and serious ICU-acquired infection.

VAP is an important complication of mechanical ventilation that should be diagnosed with the appropriate microbiological tools, treated with the appropriate antibiotics and limited to the appropriate time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VAP remains a common ICU acquired infection, but it is preventable.
the diagnosis of VAP is not a trivial issue, prevention strategies are still evolving and treatment of VAP should be limited to a short duration.
VAP is still a frequent complication of mechanical ventilation and a major contributor to ICU mortality and morbidity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VAP is a serious complication of mechanical ventilation, but it can be prevented and managed with appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
VAP is a preventable complication that can be diagnosed with a high degree of confidence and treated effectively.
VAP remains a major problem in the ICU and a major cause of mortality and morbidity.
